While not minimising the use of a human shield, six and five are not perhaps fundamentally different for these purposes; however, it's very fair of Ms. Edgerton to draw attention to that paragraph because it does contain rather more. And if that paragraph relates overall, as it appears as a reasonable inference that it does, then the whole paragraph should come out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'd rather not deal with it right away. If the parties could see whether there is an agreement. If Ms. Edgerton says, taking out 38 would be fine as far as the Prosecution is concerned, then let's be very practical and take it out, if the Defence does not oppose, and not spend any more time on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: We won't oppose to taking it out if Ms. Edgerton is prepared to make that proposal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So 38 is out as well and is also removed after it has been in evidence for a couple of minutes. It's not anymore, Madam Registrar. Then, if we could go back then not to the previous witness but, first of all, Mr. Djokanovic. I have a list in front of me which goes from P532 up to and including P548 and D37.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stewart, the registrar draws my attention to the fact that none of the Defence exhibits introduced through Witness Djokanovic have been formally tendered; that would be D37, an interview with Dragan Djokanovic, published the 25th of June, 1992; that would be D38, a witness statement, dated 12 to the 14th of February; and a D39, a witness statement dated 16, 17, and 18 of December. I noticed that Ms. Loukas announced that she would tender them. May I take it that D37, D38 and D39 are tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honours, certainly, and that does exactly reflect the helpful discussions that I had this morning with the officers of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Margetts, looking at the P list, P532 up until 548 and including that last number, Mr. Stewart, is there any objection, because I would like -- as a matter of fact, usually Madam Registrar reads out more or less the description of those documents, so I would -- since there was an exchange of what the content of those documents was this morning by e-mail, I would -- if we decide to admit them, if there are no objections, I would ask the parties to look at the list prepared by Madam Registrar to see whether the description shows any flaws, and if so, the description could be changed. That would not change the evidence, as such. Mr. Stewart, is there any objection against --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not clear what list I'm looking at. I had the e-mail this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the e-mail mentions P532 up until P548. Yes. I would like to know whether there's any objection against admission into evidence of those documents, and as we know, Madam Registrar keeps a full record of all the admitted evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You received a list which gives the numbers, the date of admission, through which witness they were admitted, who was counsel for the Prosecution at that moment, and then a description which is a bit more precise, usually, than we find it in this e-mail. If there's any comment on the precise description, that could be changed. The evidence, of course, would not change.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, Your Honour. I had no problem with the list on the e-mail, so Your Honour is inviting me, not at this moment, but if there is any discrepancy, to inform the Trial Chamber accordingly; is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. On that basis, I'm content with the list as e-mailed to me this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then P532 up to P548 and including that last number are admitted into evidence. Mr. Margetts, D37, 38, 39, any objections against ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour. Just one comment on D38. I think it was earlier described as a witness statement of 12 to 14 February. I think that was one of the dates that it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It also on the precise list, you would see it would be also the 13th of July and the 29th and the 30th of September, 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No objections, then. D37 up to and including D39 are admitted into evidence. Is there any update to be given on the matters I raised a couple of days ago? I think it was yesterday that I asked. That was about --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have -- on the question of Mr. Mandic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- and that issue was private session and confidentiality, Mr. Tieger and I did meet yesterday evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger has lobbed the ball back over to my side of the net. The only thing is that he's lobbed back exactly the ball that I'd lobbed to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So whether I'm going to play a different shot is another matter. Your Honour, I am going to consider again Mr. Tieger's proposal, but it hasn't changed, and then -- and try to inform the Trial Chamber next time we're here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, the Trial Chamber mainly wants to know not where the ball is but whether we have to give a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm doing what Your Honour's just asked me to do, Your Honour, which is report the position and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there is no solution yet. We'll wait until after the -- after Easter, and if there is no decision -- if there's no solid expectation that a solution could be reached by the party, we'll deal with the matter ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I take it that, so far as there is disagreement between us, if we are not able to resolve this matter, that we will have the opportunity of making appropriate submissions in relation to that disagreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you can even make a proposal. Together with the message that you think you could not resolve the matter, you can make a proposal for a time schedule so that we could deal with the matter within the next ten days after --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Your Honour. Thank you very much for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether it would be written or oral submissions, the Chamber will further consider. Then I think the redaction of Mr. Bjelobrk's statement would need a little bit more time. D34 and D35, the tapes, was that settled?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand from our case manager that we're still working on providing that material to the Defence. JUJDGE ORIE: Yes. In order to avoid us asking every day, would there be any idea on when we can revisit this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: She tells me the end of this week, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then after Easter we'll come back to that. Then the translation of P252, does that raise any further -- or should we wait for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, so far, I hope I've been able to answer your questions adequately, but as far as P252 is -- because I don't have the faintest recollection what it is and can't give any assistance whatever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It says that the OTP still awaits details of Defence objections to the translation of P252, and the Defence is to give details of its objections, and at that time, it says, within three weeks, and this was the 28th of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, the ball is clearly in my court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Madam Registrar, do we have any exhibits remaining from Witness 60? That's all settled. Are there any other exhibits still on our list, apart from those we dealt with? If not, I did understand that the next witness would be called tomorrow; is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, have you got any idea how much time you would need for cross-examination for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I have an idea, Your Honour, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- which, of course, I'm conscientiously willing to share. Your Honour, my idea is that I would be somewhere around two to three hours, but, Your Honour, that's -- well, not even remotely set in stone, Your Honour. I shan't be -- I'm not going to be days with him, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any response from the -- of course, I'm trying to find out whether we expect to be here still on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the -- I think it -- I'm trying to be helpful, Your Honour. I think it follows, and given that the admission of this evidence and the order in relation to cross-examination does relate to relatively confined areas, though Mr. Tieger has very helpfully indicated to me a little extra material that he wishes to refer to, which is perfectly helpful, I don't expect, Your Honour, that we're talking about exceeding a single day of hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that would include any further questions that would come up due to cross-examination? Of course, you can't -- but would there be sufficient time reserved for ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, judging by the pattern of questions and a general ratio of re-examination to cross-examination and Bench's questions, my confidence that we will finish within one day stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis, do you have a similar expectation?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I have a moment, Your Honour. I think I received an e-mail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mobile phones are banned from court, now the e- mails.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was unrelated to the immediate question. I think, based on what Mr. Stewart said and what I understand of this witness and what Mr. Tieger told me, I think it may take all day, but Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I don't think it will go into the next day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. Then the parties know that if they are not finished, they will see each other back in court on Thursday. We will adjourn until tomorrow afternoon, quarter past 2.00, in this same courtroom.
